title: Bridge the dock gap with two runner planks, then push the cart onto the truck bed
instruction: Lay the two grey runner planks across the gap between the loading dock and the truck bed, each into its pair of seats on the dock edge and the truck-bed edge. Then push the blue cart from the dock over the runners onto the truck bed, between the two yellow marks. Never lift the cart: slide it along the surfaces. Leave both runners in their seats and let go of everything.
context: A gap between a loading dock and a trailer is crossed only on a dock board or plate laid and secured first: a cart run at an open gap drops a wheel and tips, and an unsecured plate slides out under the load (OSHA 29 CFR 1910.26(c): portable dockboards must be secured so they cannot move out of a safe position). Done by hand freight, stock and material movers and by stockers (O*NET 53-7062.00, 53-7065.00); carts are pushed, not lifted. Here, with the grippers pointing down, only the left arm reaches the runners and only the right arm the cart's rear face, and the right arm can push the cart only just past the gap, so the left arm takes the push over (tilted far over, at the edge of its reach, an arm gets at more of the other's side: the relay is the natural way, not the only one). The score follows the whole trial: the path must be built before it is used, the cart never lifted, and a runner never let slide under it.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. (1) Loading dock: fixed grey blocks (concrete-coloured painted wood) spanning x 23.0 to 41.0 cm and y -30.0 to -4.0 cm, top 40.0 mm above the table. (2) Truck bed: fixed dark brown wooden blocks spanning x 23.0 to 41.0 cm and y +4.0 to +30.0 cm, top 39.0 mm above the table. Between them is an 80 mm gap (y -4.0 to +4.0 cm) open down to the table. (3) Seats: at its gap edge each side has two rebates, 50 mm wide (x 26.0 to 31.0 cm and x 34.0 to 39.0 cm) and 45 mm deep (back to y -8.5 cm on the dock, +8.5 cm on the bed), their floors 19.5 mm above the table; the two seats in the same x range face each other across the gap as a pair. Between a side's two seats is a low rib (x 31.0 to 34.0 cm, 29.5 mm high); outside them are full-height cheeks. (4) Two runner planks: loose grey aluminium boxes (hollow tube), 40 mm wide, 160 mm long and 20 mm thick, 60 g each, lying flat on the table along y left of the truck bed, end to end, one centred at x 15.0 cm, y +29.0 cm, the other at x 16.0 cm, y +46.0 cm. A runner seated in a pair spans the gap with 40 mm of each end in a seat (5 mm of play at each side and end) and its top 39.5 mm above the table: half a millimetre under the dock and over the bed, so the cart's path steps down at every seam. (5) Cart: a loose blue painted hardwood block standing in for a hand cart, 100 by 100 mm and 30 mm tall, 0.21 kg, too wide for the gripper (94 mm fully open), standing on the dock square to it, centred at x 32.5 cm, y -20.0 cm. Two seated runners each carry 30 mm of its width, one on each side of its centre; with only one, or none, it tips into the gap once its rear leaves the dock. (6) Two yellow tape marks, 25 by 120 mm and 0.5 mm thick, on the bed top along its x edges (centred at x 24.25 cm and 39.75 cm, y +21.0 cm), on either side of where the cart goes: centred at x 32.5 cm, y +21.0 cm. With the grippers pointing straight down, only the left arm reaches the runners and only the right arm the cart's rear face at the start, and pushing from behind the right arm can bring the cart's centre no farther than about y +13 cm (tilted 30 to 80 degrees, at the edge of reach, either arm gets further). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial: every control step it reads the cart's and both runners' poses and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's tool point, finger-tip point (between the tips) and opening (0 closed, 1 fully open with the fingers 94 mm apart). A runner is 'seated' when it lies flat (broad faces within 5 degrees of level), the corners of one end are inside a dock seat and those of the other end inside the facing bed seat of the same pair (1 mm tolerance), and its underside is within 2 mm of the seat floors at both ends; 'both seated' means in different pairs. The cart is 'on' a runner when their outlines overlap by 5 mm or more along x and along y and the cart's lowest point is within 3 mm of the runner's top. The cart is 'on the bed' when its whole outline is over the bed top clear of the seats (x 23.0 to 41.0 cm, y +8.5 to +30.0 cm) and its lowest point is within 2 mm of the bed top. Each gripper's 'finger zone' is every point within a radius of the segment from its finger-tip point to 38 mm back up the gripper, the radius reaching a finger's outer corner (half the current finger gap plus the finger's 10 mm thickness, and half its 40 mm width across: 60 mm fully open, 22 mm closed); 'hands off' means both finger zones are at least 30 mm from the cart and from both runners. Score 0 if at any step any part of the cart is more than 1 mm over the gap (y -4.0 to +4.0 cm) while the runners are not both seated (used before it is built, even if held up); if the cart's lowest point is below 35 mm above the table (dropped into the gap) or above 45 mm (lifted), or it tilts more than 10 degrees; if a runner's end moves more than 10 mm from where it was when the cart came onto that runner, while the cart is still on it (slid out under the load); or if the cart or a runner falls off the table (lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top). Otherwise: 1.0 if both runners are seated, the cart is on the bed with its centre within 15 mm of x 32.5 cm, y +21.0 cm and its sides within 5 degrees of square to the bed, and hands are off; 0.75 if both runners are seated and the cart is on the bed with its centre within 40 mm of that point (turned, or a gripper still at it); 0.5 if both runners are seated and the cart's centre is at y +4.0 cm or beyond (over the bed's side of the gap); 0.25 if both runners are seated; 0 in every other case. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with the cart and both runners still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, 'hands off' is taken as met. The cart and the runners are plain boxes, so either broad face may be down. In a real trial, the gap, drop, lift and tilt rules are read from a side video against 35 mm and 45 mm lines on a card standing beside the gap, a runner's movement against 10 mm scale marks along the seats, and the end state from a top photo and a tape.
fidelity: Two runner planks in rebates stand in for a dock board; the cart is a rigid block sliding on its base (no wheels), so pushing it is harder than rolling a real cart, and it falls into the gap only once its centre leaves its support, not when a wheel drops. The seams step down 0.5 mm each way. Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic, rubber-like). About 1:8 scale. Gripper heading is not read, so each finger zone is round.
reset_notes: Put both runners back flat on the table along y, end to end, centred at x 15.0 cm, y +29.0 cm and at x 16.0 cm, y +46.0 cm, and the cart back on the dock square to it, centred at x 32.5 cm, y -20.0 cm. The dock, the truck bed, their seats and the marks are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
